got_right: Ran 32 interventions against one shared control in a single fielding, so arms are directly comparable and the pooled estimate is not confounded by wave, panel or outcome wording.
Adjusted for the pre-treatment measure of each outcome (post_ap ~ arm + pre_ap) with HC2 robust SEs, which tightens estimates; the Perception gap video interval is the narrowest at [-4.3, -0.4].
Reported the whole arm table and hedged the lone p = 0.019 result against 64 uncorrected tests, rather than presenting one arm as a winner.
Pooled across arms (-0.8 points, 95% CI [-1.4, -0.2]) and found no pooled movement in support for undemocratic practices (-0.015, CI [-0.044, 0.014]).

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Most arms had 48-150 respondents against a control of 229, so arm-level intervals are about 6-8 points wide and cannot exclude effects larger than the pooled -0.8. Only the Perception gap video (n = 641) was estimated with any precision.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Standard errors of 1.3-3.2 on the feeling thermometer for nearly all arms; control n = 229; Cross-partisan dialogue guide CI [-8.0, 4.5].

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Interventions differ in format, length, topic and target, so 32 arms bundle many features. A null or a hit cannot be tied to a mechanism, and one arm clearing p < 0.05 among 32 tests is about what chance produces.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Perception gap video p = 0.019 uncorrected; next arms are 'What makes an American' video p = 0.059 and Patriotic article p = 0.100.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Outcomes were measured immediately after exposure, with a single thermometer-based measure and one undemocratic-practices scale. Durability and behaviour are unobserved, and immediate shifts may reflect demand.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Limitations: outcomes measured right after exposure; the thermometer gap is the only affect measure.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Analysis kept 4,547 of 6,086 respondents, and 3,825 and 3,953 entered the two models. Differential attrition across arms, plus the dropped chatbot arm, could bias the contrasts. Only Democrats and Republicans were retained.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: N = 3825 (H1) and N = 3953 (H2) versus 6,086 raw; arm T33 excluded after technical failures.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: No pre-registration, so analytic choices (weights, exclusions, pooling) are post hoc, and the robustness checks add little: the completers re-fit showed only full-sample rows and the Democrat-interaction tests are too imprecise to say anything.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Registration status 'none'; E2 interaction SEs of 3-10 points; 0 of 32 interactions at p < 0.05.

debates.label: Do prejudice-reduction effects carry through to downstream political outcomes?
debates.position_a: Brief interventions can shift intergroup affect, and that shift should extend to political attitudes such as support for undemocratic practices or violence.
debates.position_b: Affective shifts are small and local, and may not transfer to democratic attitudes, or to settings beyond the United States.
debates.what_this_study_says: Leans to position b, weakly: a small thermometer reduction (-0.8) coexisted with no pooled change in undemocratic-practices support (-0.015). The intervals are wide and the outcomes were measured immediately, so the study cannot settle it.

briefs.title: Perception gap correction with a mechanism manipulation and delayed follow-up
briefs.question: Does correcting misperceptions of the other party reduce affective polarization through changed meta-perceptions, and does the effect persist?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes the power and design problems by concentrating on the only arm with signal and by isolating its mechanism, adding a delayed outcome to address the immediate-measurement limit.
briefs.design_sketch: Four arms: control, the Perception gap video, a placebo video of the same length and format on a non-political topic, and a perception-gap statistics-only text. Measure perceived out, party gap and the feeling thermometer, plus undemocratic-practices support, immediately and again after 2-4 weeks. Recruit partisan US adults with pre-treatment measures of both outcomes. Mediation is tested via the shift in perceived outparty views.

power_target.basis: Observed Perception gap video effect of -2.3 points (SE 0.995 at n = 641); sizing to detect about -1.7 at 80% power allows for winner's-curse shrinkage.

briefs.title: Affect-to-democratic-attitude transfer test
briefs.question: Do thermometer reductions produce changes in support for undemocratic practices, or are the two outcomes independent?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Addresses the measurement failure: the original had a null on undemocratic-practices support with no way to tell whether affect failed to transfer or the intervention was too weak.
briefs.design_sketch: Randomize to the Perception gap video, a Patriotic article, or control. Use a stronger intervention variant (video plus recall task) to produce a larger affect shift. Measure affect, undemocratic-practices support and a behavioural proxy (willingness to donate to a cross-party group). Test whether the affect change predicts downstream change using instrumental or mediation analysis. Positions differ: transfer predicts downstream change proportional to affect change; independence predicts none even with a large affect shift.

power_target.basis: Undemocratic-practices pooled CI [-0.044, 0.014] and arm SEs of 0.05-0.12; 900 per arm detects about 0.09 on that scale.

briefs.title: Perception gap video across partisanship and sample
briefs.question: Does the Perception gap video effect hold across partisan identity, strength of partisanship and a second sample source?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Addresses the sample and framing limits: the original was one Lucid panel, only partisans, with heterogeneity tests too imprecise to interpret.
briefs.design_sketch: Two-arm design (Perception gap video vs control) fielded in a Lucid and a probability-based or alternative panel, stratified by Democrat, Republican and independent leaners. Outcomes are the feeling thermometer and undemocratic-practices support, with pre-measures. Estimate treatment effects by party and sample and test interactions.
briefs.moderator_or_condition: Party (Democrat, Republican, independent) and sample source (Lucid vs second panel)

power_target.basis: Interaction contrasts need roughly 2x the SE of the main effect; observed SE 0.995 at n = 641 implies detecting about 2 points in subgroups at around 750 per cell.

verdict: A follow-up is worth running, but narrowly. The 32-arm screen found a pooled -0.8 point shift, one nominal hit (Perception gap video, -2.3, p = 0.019, uncorrected and post hoc), and nothing on undemocratic practices. Run the Perception gap correction with a mechanism manipulation and delayed follow-up first: it replicates the single signal at adequate power, adds a placebo, and tests persistence. The affect-to-democratic-attitude transfer test and the cross-party, cross-sample test follow once the effect is confirmed.
